history.period: c. 18th century (~250 years old, per the Haryana government tourism page)
history.summary: The Devi Temple of Panipat is the Shri Devi Mandir on Devi Mandir Road, Tehsil Camp, Panipat 132103 - a Durga temple prominently listed on the Haryana government's official tourism page (panipat.gov.in). It stands on the bank of a former drought pond that has been converted into a park used for morning/evening walks; a Ramlila has been staged in the park for about 100 years during Navratri. Per the government page, the temple is about 250 years old and its history is tied to the 18th-century Maratha presence: Sadashivrao Bhau camped at Panipat for nearly two months before the Third Battle of Panipat (1761) against Ahmad Shah Abdali, and local belief holds that he found the Goddess idol on the bank of the pond and built the temple (the idol is said to have 'returned' overnight to its original spot when moved). The temple has since been rebuilt in good modern architecture and houses idols of all Hindu gods and goddesses plus a Yaga Shala. CONFLICTS: the inheritage.foundation guide attributes the temple to 'Maratha Sardar Bhaskar Rao Pandit' and calls the goddess Bhadrakali, while panipat.gov.in credits the Sadashivrao Bhau tradition and says Goddess Durga - both noted without resolution. The temple is distinct from a newer 'Devi Temple' listing at Seenk, Panipat.

town_description: Panipat is a historic city in Haryana on NH-44 (G.T. Road), about 90 km north of Delhi. It is famous as the site of the three battles of Panipat (1526, 1556, 1761) and is today India's 'Textile City' and 'City of Weavers', the biggest centre for quality blankets and carpets.
